competitor-positioning.name: Reeves' Unique Selling Proposition (USP) — 3-Part Test

competitor-positioning.name: The Preemptive Claim (Schlitz / Live Steam)

competitor-positioning.one_line: In categories where products are functionally identical, the first brand to articulate a common process or ingredient owns it in the prospect's mind — Schlitz claimed 'every bottle washed with live steam' first and owned 'purity'.

competitor-positioning.name: USP Pre-emption & The Deceptive Differential Test
competitor-positioning.one_line: Once a USP is established via penetration, a competitor copying it only advertises the leader; the moat is penetration not truth. The Deceptive Differential Test checks whether the claimed difference is actually perceivable after purchase.

competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising (Ch. 9); Hopkins; Sugarman
competitor-positioning.one_line: An ad must focus all selling power into one dominant concept like a burning glass focuses sunlight; the consumer remembers one thing. One reader, one big idea, one promise, one offer.

competitor-positioning.name: The Multi-Million Dollar Error (don't change a winning campaign)

competitor-positioning.name: Principle of Dispersion (Reach Before Frequency)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Reaching more people once beats reaching fewer many times — first exposure has highest marginal impact, subsequent exposures diminish rapidly; prioritize new reach over saturating existing audiences.

competitor-positioning.one_line: The mind organizes brands on a ladder (one per category), rejects info that contradicts what's there, holds room for ~3 brands; positioning is what you do to the prospect's mind, not the product. Perception is reality.

scaling.one_line: PGS in reverse: if 7-day CPA exceeds target, decrease budget by a defined % (typically 20%). Safety net. Meta can push/pull budget ~75% on any day regardless.

scaling.name: Three Reasons Scale Breaks
scaling.one_line: Scaling answers one question: can we spend more tomorrow? If no, only 3 reasons: bad unit economics (GPT = AOV-CPA too low), funnel imbalance (4Pi shows all ads same position), cash constraints (make each dollar work harder, lift second-purchase rate).
scaling.best_query: three reasons scale breaks unit economics funnel imbalance cash constraints can we spend more tomorrow

scaling.name: Scaling Mindset Farmer vs Hunter (Andromeda)
scaling.one_line: ROAS creates hunters (only as good as today's kill, 3-5 bad days = out of business); PSM creates farmers (compounding predictable revenue, weather volatility on rolling revenue). Post-Andromeda needs clarity/coherence, not volume/chaos.
scaling.best_query: scaling mindset farmer vs hunter Andromeda think bigger clarity not volume

scaling.name: Fractional Banking
scaling.one_line: Once rolling repeat-purchase revenue arrives, borrow against future revenue to invest more aggressively in acquisition today. PSM (not ROAS) enables this via future-cash-flow accounting. Model with a fractional CFO before going negative on CPA.
scaling.best_query: fractional banking borrow against future revenue rolling repeat purchase cash flow scale negative CPA

scaling.name: More Better New Scaling Framework
scaling.one_line: Before adding a new acquisition method: More (do more of what works), Better (improve scripts/targeting/follow-up), New (only after maximizing More and Better). Most jump to New prematurely, abandoning winners.
scaling.best_query: More Better New scaling framework Hormozi sequence maximize before new method

scaling.name: Reeves' Principle of Dispersion
scaling.one_line: Reach beats frequency, better to show one ad to 10 people than to 1 person 10 times. Diminishing returns set in fast; each new person has full response potential. When scaling, prioritize new audiences over saturating existing ones.
scaling.best_query: Reeves principle of dispersion reach over frequency Reality in Advertising new audiences

scaling.name: Drayton Bird's Square Root Principle
scaling.source: Drayton Bird (Commonsense Direct and Digital Marketing)
scaling.one_line: A quarter-page ad pulls ~half the response of a full-page ad, so it's ~2x more cost-effective per response. Smaller media spaces can win on cost-per-acquisition. Direct-response media is judged by cost per response, not cost per thousand.
scaling.best_query: Drayton Bird square root principle smaller ads cost per response Commonsense Direct Marketing

scaling.name: Creative Diversity as a Scaling Mechanism
scaling.one_line: When budget increases break performance, 4Pi usually shows all ads in the same funnel position. Restore balance: add video (top-funnel) to image-heavy accounts where scale fails; add images (bottom-funnel) to video-heavy accounts where CPA climbs. Diversity = variety of messages, not volume of ads.
scaling.best_query: creative diversity as a scaling mechanism funnel balance video image 4Pi same position

scaling.name: ROAS Targets Vertical vs Horizontal (Add-One Rule)
scaling.source: Easy A Media (EAM) scaling SOP (no book author)
scaling.one_line: Target ROAS = break-even ROAS + 1 (BE 1.6 -> target 2.6). Break-even ROAS derives from gross-profit margin. Can scale slightly below target if added spend nets more profit. PSM ultimately replaces ROAS because it incorporates LTV and COGS.
scaling.best_query: ROAS target add one to break-even rule vertical horizontal scaling gross profit margin

scaling.name: EAM Scaling Protocol & Decision Tree
scaling.one_line: Hitting target KPI? If yes -> in scaling protocol (48-72h above target = scale every 24h)? Or new reason (new winning ad/offer/LP)? Or limited-time promo (skip the wait)? Confirm 60%+ click-based, then bump 20% flat (50-100% when 50%+ above KPI). If no -> below break-even 24-48h? Scale down 20%.

scaling.name: Levels of Scaling (Zero-to-50K to 100K/day)

scaling.name: Scaling Click-Based Data Gate
scaling.one_line: Before any scale-up verify 60%+ of purchases are click-based (7-day-click/1-day-view). If >60% view-through, performance may be phantom attribution, consider 7-day-click-only before scaling. Scaling on view-through-heavy data tanks the account.

scaling.name: Spend Redistribution Framework (Don't Kill the Top Spender)
scaling.one_line: Before turning off a high-spend ad, ask: if spend redistributes to other ads, would they hold a better ROAS at higher spend? Bumping budget drops ROAS 5-25%, so the top spender (lower ROAS, most purchases) is usually your best scaling asset. Only kill it when ROAS is so low (~0.78x) redistribution clearly wins.

scaling.name: Frequency as Prospecting-vs-Retargeting Proxy
scaling.one_line: In broad CBO campaigns frequency reveals prospecting vs disguised retargeting: low (1.0-1.5) = prospecting (reliable scaling signal); high (2.5+) = retargeting. High-ROAS + high-frequency = ROAS inflated by retargeting, don't scale on it. Killing a top prospecting ad starves retargeting and collapses performance within a week.

scaling.name: Would It Hold at 3X Budget? (Mental Model)
scaling.one_line: When a low-spend ad shows very high ROAS, ask: if I put 3x budget on it, would it hold? Almost always no, a $50-spend 10X-ROAS ad is statistically insignificant, not a winner. Don't scale based on it.

scaling.name: Hero Offer First Scale vs Second Scale
scaling.one_line: First Scale = cheapest CPA, attracts discount hunters/one-time buyers (builds nothing). Second Scale = best customer journey, high-LTV repeat buyers and advocates (builds the business). Identify via Customer Journey Insights + PSM filter (1.3+, 40%+ repeat, <65 days), then build all creative testing around it.

scaling.name: Minimum Daily Spend & Creative Hamster Wheel
scaling.one_line: Minimum daily spend = amount you'll spend regardless of performance ($50-100/day for algorithm data; budget 1-2+ months). The creative hamster wheel: post-Andromeda, every new ad launches bottom-funnel and steals warm-audience attention from winners, destabilizing the account. scaling.name: Margin vs Volume Two Paths
scaling.one_line: High-margin makes more per sale but grows slowly; high-volume makes less per sale but grows fast. Neither is right, they build different machines. Choose your scaling game consciously because target ROAS, aggression and acceptable CPA all flow from it.

scaling.name: Going Negative on CPA (LTV-Funded Acquisition)
